original_uncoded_notes_exact.source_first_notes: Dust returns from Elroad with actual compensation and expects to pay his dream-shop tab and enjoy leisure. A quoted earlier exchange reveals he increased payment through an implied publicity threat; his readily-paid/negotiation label is contradicted by the prince's trembling and Leen's explicit extortion appraisal. He privately expects emphasizing Kazuma to divert royal retaliation onto his friend. Leen actually takes the full bag for failed-commission compensation and the extended dragon-coach rental, saying Dust delegated negotiations to Taylor and ignored the terms. He privately concedes those facts. Taking funds is actual; her proposed remittance to Rein is not yet performed. A later timeskip mentions other main-party incidents without supplying whole independent episodes. Dust claims he knows saving/budgeting words but not meaning and refuses work except easy or very profitable work; an announced treasure-island opportunity immediately meets that stated condition rather than disproving an unconditional never-work vow. All four actually rush to the giant Genbu with borrowed mining kit, using Keith's optical/aim skills and hook rope to gain a good place. Mining has real disguised-monster risk, explaining why untrained residents are absent. Dust refuses a known adventurer's requested help for extra share, explicitly appraising that man as able to win though delayed. Leen and Taylor actually help. When Dust and Keith meet a larger mimic, others return their selfish reasoning and Keith abandons Dust under a supportive-sounding line. Dust actually fights with sword and pickaxe, repels it and recovers the delay, but exhaustion sends him to the stable. A dream then presents the important unnamed woman at dragon stables: his rough waking voice is corrected into formal speech and 俺 into 私, she differentiates official/public conduct from informal freedom, he refuses the requested dragon ride as dangerous and knowingly avoids a shared painful topic. The scene cuts before the rank phrase is completed; do not independently identify her from ???art or pretraining. In the present he mistakes Leen for her on waking, then invents a knight-imitation/marriage-scam explanation to conceal the lapse. Leen rejects the performance, and he privately admits the deception and fatigue, wondering why such dreams have become rarer. She reports Yunyun sought him only after she noticed the hesitant circling and asked; his initial claim of improved initiative receives this correction. Yunyun's actual purpose remains unread.

Refusing help under confident encouragement becomes the same rhetoric used against Dust when he needs help; he does eventually win but pays in exhaustion.
A dream's old formal role leaks into waking speech, then is deliberately covered as a crude new scam performance.
An apparent report of Yunyun's new social initiative turns out to depend on Leen initiating the contact.

original_uncoded_notes_exact.source_first_notes: Yunyun's hesitant private request is first misread as a confession, which she explicitly denies while asserting her right to choose and reporting reputational damage from association with Dust. He privately notices her unusual behavior specifically because she is normally more natural alone with him. He mocks Vanir's elevated address, then apologizes before blaming her for the delay he caused. While she is distracted, he assigns his food bill to her and exploits a perfunctory uninformed response; he explicitly can afford the meal after the Genbu profit. Her actual request is a front-line partner for the two-person Crimson Demon chief trial, not marriage. Dust initially refuses because he has money and dislikes work, demands increasingly extravagant introductions and later privately recognizes the trial may be difficult. Leen criticizes him but cannot fill the stated front-line role herself. He says he might consider it if she has no one, expects Kazuma will help, then reverses toward joining when Leen reminds him of an earlier reported abundance of attractive single women. A daily Explosion renews his aversion and he settles back against going. No actual trial or current immediate coercive danger has yet been shown. At a bar Dust considers extorting an unfamiliar handsome robed man, asks Kazuma whether they know each other and proceeds after a no. The man names himself Duke, and Dust initially mistakes composure for concealed fear. Actual oppressive power then changes Dust's appraisal; to save face before other customers, he recasts the extortion as an adventurer test that includes buying a drink for those who resist. He really orders the drink and leaves, then complains to Kazuma of the unexpected expense. His comparison to demon-executive strength is his appraisal, not a confirmed rank or identity. Later he interrupts dressed-up Darkness with real name/status despite her attempted denial, receives money and withdraws, then joins Kazuma/Aqua watching. He guesses a courting contest and recruits Small to humiliate Duke, not knowing the full underlying plan. She expressly refuses and identifies his pride-baiting tactic as ineffective, which he recognizes as learning. Once he mentions an overheard wish to marry Wiz and make her leave the shop, Small imagines a vacancy and romance with Vanir, insists on helping even as Dust loses interest, and develops her own plan. Her stated professional theory for a modest presentation is hers, and Dust accepts it rather than independently verifying it. Immediately before entry she clarifies she intends to bring Duke and Wiz together, not seduce Duke herself; he protests but she proceeds. Duke detects her demonic nature, her polite performance collapses into malformed panicked speech, and Dust prepares to intervene if exposure makes trouble. The last paragraph is Duke's question whether Vanir sent her; no actual instruction by Vanir or response has yet been read.
